reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring lower-limb items from imaging rather than function.
name: Modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association Score

version.label: mJOA, clinician-rated (Benzel et al. 1991), 0–18
version.detail: Upper-limb motor 0–5, lower-limb motor 0–7, upper-limb sensation 0–3, micturition 0–3. Severity bands from Tetreault/Fehlings (2017). Not the original JOA (1975, 17 points) and not the patient-derived mJOA.

purpose: Clinician-rated severity of degenerative cervical myelopathy.

options.label: Unable to move hands
Unable to eat with a spoon but able to move hands
Unable to button shirt but able to eat with a spoon
Able to button shirt with great difficulty
Able to button shirt with slight difficulty
No dysfunction
Complete loss of motor and sensory function
Sensory preservation without ability to move legs
Able to move legs but unable to walk
Able to walk on a flat floor with a walking aid
Able to walk up and/or down stairs with a hand rail
Moderate to significant lack of stability, but walks up and/or down stairs without a hand rail
Mild lack of stability; walks unaided with smooth reciprocation
No dysfunction
Complete loss of hand sensation
Severe sensory loss or pain
Mild sensory loss
No sensory loss
Unable to micturate voluntarily
Marked difficulty with micturition
Mild to moderate difficulty with micturition
Normal micturition

resultStates.label: Severe myelopathy
resultStates.detail: Correlate with examination, imaging and progression according to local practice.

resultStates.label: No dysfunction measured
resultStates.summary: mJOA 18: no dysfunction measured at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Does not exclude imaging cord compression or subtle signs.

clinicalContext.text: The standard clinician-rated severity measure for degenerative cervical myelopathy in Western practice.

clinicalInsights.text: Report the domain scores with the total; motor items carry 12 of 18 points.
Compare serial scores using the same version (mJOA and JOA are not interchangeable).

limitations.text: Not interchangeable with the original JOA score (1975) or the patient-derived mJOA.

limitations: Upper-limb sensation only; lower-limb and trunk sensation are not scored.
Function can be limited by non-myelopathic conditions.

confounders.factor: Peripheral neuropathy or carpal tunnel syndrome

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Rate of progression on its own.

guideSections.what: An 18-point clinician-rated scale of upper- and lower-limb motor function, hand sensation and micturition.
guideSections.whenToUse: Severity grading and follow-up of degenerative cervical myelopathy.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score each of the four domains from history and examination. Add the four domain scores.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Used with examination findings, imaging and the time course.

sources.citation: Benzel EC, Lancon J, Kesterson L, Hadden T. Cervical laminectomy and dentate ligament section for cervical spondylotic myelopathy. J Spinal Disord. 1991;4(3):286-295.

Tetreault L, Kopjar B, Nouri A, et al. The modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association scale: establishing criteria for mild, moderate and severe impairment in patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy. Eur Spine J. 2017;26(1):78-84.

licensing.note: Reproduced in open-access literature. The patient-derived mJOA (myelopathy.org, reproduced with permission) is a separate instrument and is not implemented.
